title: Kooky Yeasty Turkish Sausage Flatbread
description: A yeasty and gooey Turkish dish featuring Andouille sausage, double fried for a crispy exterior and a soft interior, perfect for a crowd, and can be adapted to be paleo friendly.

ingredients.name: active dry yeast
ingredients.notes: make sure to use warm water to activate

instructions: In a large mixing bowl, combine the warm water and yeast, stirring to dissolve the yeast, then let it sit for 5 minutes.
Add the flour, salt, black pepper, and garlic powder to the bowl, mixing until a shaggy dough forms.
Knead the dough for 5 minutes until it becomes smooth and elastic, then place it in a greased bowl, cover it with a damp cloth, and let it rise in a warm place for 1 hour.
Preheat the oil in a deep frying pan to 350 degrees Fahrenheit.
Punch down the dough and divide it into 4 equal pieces, rolling each piece into a ball and then flattening it into a disk shape.
Double fry the Andouille sausage slices, first frying them at 325 degrees Fahrenheit for 2 minutes, then increasing the heat to 375 degrees Fahrenheit and frying for an additional 2 minutes.
Place a few slices of the fried sausage onto each flatbread, leaving a 1/2 inch border around the edges.
Fold the edges of the flatbread up over the sausage to form a crust, brushing the edges with a little water to seal.
Fry the flatbreads in the hot oil for 2-3 minutes on each side, until golden brown and crispy.
Remove the flatbreads from the oil and place them on a paper towel lined plate to drain excess oil.
